rationale: This conference paper addresses technical demand and energy load forecasting tools to optimize water utility pumping schedules and electricity/natural gas procurement costs. Mention of energy tariff structures refers to wholesale electricity pricing paid by the utility rather than rules or tariffs governing household or community water service access, leaving no relevant exposure or service-access outcome (E06).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain readings because the paper focuses entirely on technical pumping load forecasting and wholesale electricity/fuel procurement optimization for utility operations rather than legal, administrative or institutional governance of household water or sanitation service access.

evidence_quotes.quote: Utilizing energy and demand forecasting as a tool to develop energy procurement strategies

The capability to effectively forecast demand profile and schedule production can be beneficially used to guide the utility to procure energy products (electricity, diesel or natural gas) in a manner designed to contain costs.
